title: Palindrome Pairs
description: Brute force to optimized: checking every ordered pair directly versus a reversed trie tagged with palindrome-prefix information.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given an array of distinct strings words, return all index pairs [i, j] (with i not equal to j) such that concatenating words[i] and words[j] produces a palindrome.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","words array of distinct strings"],["Output","All ordered index pairs [i,j] where words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome"],["Goal","Use a trie of reversed words, tagged with palindrome-suffix information, to avoid checking every pair directly"],["Constraints","Up to 5000 words, each up to 300 characters"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Concatenation of two words forms a palindrome\"","One word's prefix must mirror the other word's suffix; reversing words into a trie exposes this mirroring as a trie walk"],["\"Distinct words, potentially many of them\"","A trie built from reversed words, annotated with palindrome-suffix indices at each node, checks all candidates for one word in one walk"]]}

blocks.text: If words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome, then either words[j] is the exact reverse of a PREFIX of words[i] (with the remaining suffix of words[i] itself being a palindrome), or words[i] is the exact reverse of words[j] entirely (equal lengths), or a symmetric case with roles swapped. Building a trie from words REVERSED, then walking each word forward through that trie, surfaces exactly these mirroring relationships.

blocks.title: Analogy: Finding Words That Complete Each Other Into a Mirror
blocks.text: Picture a shelf of reversed word cards. Walking a candidate word forward, letter by letter, along these reversed cards finds every other word whose reversal lines up as a matching prefix, with the leftover piece needing to be checked for being a palindrome by itself.

blocks.caption: Reverse each word into a trie; walking the OTHER word forward through this trie finds candidates whose remaining piece is a palindrome

blocks.text: Result: [[0,1],[1,0],[2,4],[3,2]]. "abcd"+"dcba" = "abcddcba" is a palindrome. "lls"+"s" = "llss"? Actually "s"+"sssll"="ssssll" is not; but "lls"+"sssll" combos are checked directly by the algorithm, yielding these exact pairs.

Before checking every ordered pair of words directly (concatenating and testing for a palindrome), notice that reversing words into a trie converts "does some word's reversal match a prefix of this word" into a direct trie walk, checking many candidates simultaneously.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome exactly when either words[j] equals the reverse of a prefix of words[i] (with the leftover suffix of words[i] itself being a palindrome), or the mirrored case with words[i] as the reversed prefix of words[j].

Observation 2: Building a trie from every word REVERSED lets walking a candidate word FORWARD through the trie locate every other word whose reversal exactly matches some prefix walked so far.

Observation 3: At each trie node visited while walking a word forward, if that node marks the END of some other reversed word, check whether the REMAINING suffix of the current word (from this point to its end) is itself a palindrome, if so a valid pair is found.

Observation 4: After the walk reaches the end of the current word, any reversed word extending further in the trie whose CONSUMED prefix so far is itself a palindrome also yields a valid pair (the symmetric case), which is why each trie node also stores a list of word indices whose corresponding leftover prefix is a palindrome.
This leads to building a trie from reversed words (tagging palindrome-prefix indices along the way), then walking each word forward through the trie to collect all valid pairs.
Try every ordered pair of distinct words, concatenate them directly, and check whether the result is a palindrome.
Why the code is written this way

items: Checking every ordered pair directly implements the definition simply.
This costs O(n squared times word length), far too slow for up to 5000 words; a reversed trie finds all matches for one word in a single walk instead.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared times word length) for all pairwise concatenation and palindrome checks.
Space: O(word length) per concatenation.
Limitation: a trie of reversed words, annotated with palindrome-prefix indices, checks all candidates for a given word in one walk proportional to that word's length, not the full word count.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Build a trie by inserting every word REVERSED. While inserting word idx, at each remaining unconsumed prefix (before following the next reversed character), check if that PREFIX of the original word (from the very start up to the current point) is a palindrome; if so, record idx in that trie node's list. Mark the final node of each reversed word with that word's own index. Then for each word, walk it FORWARD through the trie: at every node passed through that marks the end of some OTHER word, check if the current word's REMAINING suffix (from here to its end) is a palindrome, if so a valid pair. After the walk (either completing the word or running out of trie path), also check the current trie node's stored palindrome-prefix indices for further valid pairs.
Build a trie of reversed words with palindrome-tagging during insertion; then walk each word forward through the trie to collect all valid pairs.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Action"],"rows":[["Insert \"abcd\" reversed (\"dcba\") into trie","Marks the final node with index 0"],["Insert \"dcba\" reversed (\"abcd\") into trie","Marks the final node with index 1"],["Walk \"abcd\" forward through the trie","Follows a-b-c-d, reaching the node marked index 1 (from inserting \"dcba\" reversed); remaining suffix from this point is empty, trivially a palindrome: pair [0,1] found"],["Walk \"dcba\" forward","Symmetric: pair [1,0] found"]]}

blocks.text: Reversing words during trie construction means that walking a DIFFERENT word forward through the trie retraces exactly the reversed characters of some stored word, character for character; wherever this walk passes a node marking the end of another word, the remaining unconsumed suffix of the current word is exactly the piece that would need to be a palindrome for the concatenation to work out, which is checked directly. The stored palindrome-prefix lists handle the symmetric case where the current word runs out before the stored word does, but the consumed prefix (of the stored, longer reversed word) already forms a palindrome on its own.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(total characters times average word length) for construction and querying (palindrome checks cost up to word length each).
Space: O(total characters) for the trie.

blocks.text: Palindrome Pairs is one of the more advanced trie applications: reversing words to expose mirror relationships, tagged with palindrome-prefix bookkeeping during construction.

items: Forgetting the symmetric case (checking the trie node's stored palindrome-prefix indices after the main walk), missing valid pairs where the current word is shorter than the matched stored word.
Double-counting a word paired with itself; explicitly excluding i equal to j is required.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["An empty string is present in the words list","It pairs with every other palindrome word in the list, in both orders."],["No two words can ever concatenate into a palindrome","Returns an empty list."]]}

blocks.text: Explicitly stating "reversing exposes the mirror relationship needed for a palindrome concatenation, and a trie finds all matches for one word in a single walk" demonstrates the key insight clearly.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "find all pairs of strings whose concatenation is a palindrome", think: a trie of reversed words, tagged with palindrome-prefix information, walked forward per word.

items: How would you solve this using a hash map of reversed words plus a palindrome-prefix precomputation instead of an explicit trie, achieving a similar complexity with a simpler structure?

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The pairwise-check approach costs O(n squared times word length); the reversed-trie approach costs roughly O(total characters times average word length), the standard efficient solution for this hard trie problem.

items: Pattern: a trie built from reversed words, annotated with palindrome-prefix indices, to expose mirror relationships.
Core Idea: words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome exactly when one word's reversal matches a prefix of the other, with the leftover piece itself being a palindrome.
Time: O(n squared times word length) for the brute force, O(total characters times average word length) for the trie approach.
Space: O(word length) for the brute force, O(total characters) for the trie approach.
Most Important Observation: reversing words converts palindrome-concatenation checks into a trie-walkable mirror relationship.
Interview Difficulty: a hard, advanced trie application.
One line memory trick: reverse into a trie, walk forward, check leftover pieces for palindromes.
